Commercial feature

STARR ★ SCHAEFER Report

Your monthly go-to for real estate market trends, market stats & mortgage money matters

Piedmont Post · October 7, 2026 · 2 min read

Happy Fall, all!

THE VALUE OF LOCAL REPRESENTATION:

An exceptionally strong class of motivated buyers is fueling heavy demand in Piedmont right now, proving that the fall market remains a fantastic opportunity to sell before the season winds down for winter. This localized window offers sellers a great time to achieve excellent results with careful preparation and local expertise.

For buyers, navigating our fast-moving, highly competitive market is always easier with local representation by your side. Working with a local agent brings a few distinct advantages:

  • Exclusive Insight: Local agents are often the first to know about unique opportunities around town, including quiet, off-market properties.
  • Intimate Inventory Knowledge: They tour the inventory firsthand and know recent neighborhood sales that make good comparables, often with in-depth knowledge of properties and their condition to help put a new listing’s true value into perspective.
  • Good Neighbors: Over the years, local agents build real friendships and trust with colleagues across different brokerages. When things get competitive, that mutual respect and track record of smooth closings can be the comfort a listing agent needs to help choose your offer.

MORTGAGE MONEY

Our “go-to” Mortgage Money Broker, BRADY THOMAS, LA SALLE MORTGAGE, has this to share this month:

Mortgage rates have moved sharply higher over the past month, and last week the Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time in more than three years. With inflation heating back up, energy costs rising and the war with Iran continuing, homeowners should be prepared for mortgage rates to stay higher for longer.

From my seat as a mortgage lender, higher rates are becoming just as much a seller problem as a buyer problem. I’m talking with more buyers who recognize that when a home needs work, has been sitting, or is priced too aggressively, they have leverage. Instead of simply asking for a lower price, buyers are more frequently negotiating seller credits that can be used to lower their mortgage rate or cover closing costs. This is often the most effective way to bridge the affordability gap. Sellers with the best homes may not need to make these concessions, but everyone else should understand that buyers will increasingly look to sellers for help with the economic pain in the mortgage markets.
